newsitem.title: PERU: Peru gov't to set anchovy fishing ban by Monday.
newsitem.headline: Peru gov't to set anchovy fishing ban by Monday.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Wednesday it was "four or five days" away from setting a ban on anchovy fishing because the industry had fished almost all of its November to January quota of three million tonnes.
"We are above 2.8 million tonnes, which means a ban will be decreed in four or five days," Fisheries' Minister Carlos Boggiano Sanchez said in an interview with local radio station, CPN.
The ban will only have effect in the country's northern and central waters because "in the south practically nothing has been fished" of the 200,000 tonnes quota, Boggiano added.
The minister did not say if the government would impose a ban on sardine fishing. The industry had a quota for sardines of 200,000 tonnes throughout all waters in the November to January period.
Peru is the world's second-largest producer of fishmeal, made principally from anchovy.
The government normally imposes two temporary bans on fishing per year, around October and February, to preserve stock.
